title: Affinity-based eval suite + staged apply for batching/caching cost recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an affinity-driven evaluation harness and staged apply workflow to safely recommend and roll out batching/caching configuration changes that reduce token cost without degrading output quality. The approach focuses on behavioral anchors (clustered “affinities” of prompts and usage slices) rather than single golden prompts, combined with sequential statistical checks and automated shadow/apply lanes to detect regressions early and enable fast, safe rollback.
goals: Produce a runnable eval suite that maps a candidate batching/caching config to quality and cost signals per affinity cluster
Define deterministic acceptance thresholds (both semantic and behavioral) per affinity and implement sequential testing to avoid false positives from small sample sizes
Implement a staged apply pipeline: dry-run -> shadow-apply -> 1% canary -> 10% ramp -> full, with automated rollback triggers and manual override hooks
Expose per-customer and per-route visibility for trials and ensure auditability for Private/Dedicated deployments
acceptance_criteria: Eval suite runs end-to-end on CI and returns per-affinity cost delta and quality deltas (ROUGE, embedding similarity, classifier/regression logits)
Acceptance decision computed using pre-defined thresholds and sequential p-value corrections (e.g., alpha-spending) and persisted in run metadata
Shadow-apply mode mirrors production traffic to the candidate config without affecting responses; resource accounting and cost delta estimated within 5% of real apply
Automated rollback triggers: semantic similarity drop > 0.06 average across top-5 affinites OR increase in customer-facing error rate > 0.5% OR human-labeled regression rate > 0.2%
Runbook and dashboard links present in the Linear ticket; incident checklist and contact list validated with on-call
End-to-end PR (runtime + console + control-plane) merged and deployed to staging, with smoke tests green
design_decisions: Use affinity clustering of prompt corpus (k-proto with embedding centroids) to form 8-12 buckets per workload — gives better coverage than single golden set
Combine semantic (embedding cosine) and behavioral (token counts, stop-token rate, rerank ordering changes) metrics for a composite quality score
Adopt a conservative alpha-spending sequential test to allow ongoing monitoring during ramp without inflating Type I error
Shadow-apply will be implemented as a non-blocking path that duplicates requests; no user-visible delay added in canary lanes
Manual approval required before >=10% traffic ramp for Hosted and Dedicated; automatic rolling allowed for test tenants
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: small-volume affinities will produce noisy statistics. Mitigation: aggregate similar low-volume affinites and enforce minimum sample windows (N>=200) before acceptance

Risk: semantic metrics miss subtle instruction-following regressions. Mitigation: include targeted instruction-following golden prompts per affinity and a small human audit loop for first two canaries
Risk: resource overcommit during shadow-apply. Mitigation: rate-limit mirrored traffic and cap parallel shadow workers; include cost alerts into SLO dashboard
Risk: false rollback oscillation. Mitigation: add hysteresis windows and require sustained breach for T minutes before triggering full rollback
implementation_plan: 1) Data: generate affinity clusters from historical request corpus and curate seed golden prompts per affinity (owner: data infra)
2) Eval harness: implement per-affinity runner that computes semantic + behavioral metrics and a composite score (owner: runtime team)
3) Statistical layer: add sequential-test library and decision engine into control plane (owner: platform)
4) Shadow/Canary flow: wire shadow duplication and canary traffic splitter; surface run metadata to console (owner: control-plane + console)
5) Rollout logic: implement automated rollback hooks and manual approval workflow; add runbook and alerts (owner: ops)
6) QA: run against 3 customer-like workloads and perform human audit on first two canaries before production rollout
metrics_to_track: per-affinity composite quality delta (baseline vs candidate)
end-to-end token cost delta and projected monthly savings
frequency of automated rollbacks and reason codes
